yomizaka.detail: Upload the file, the findings come back.
It shows what it finds, not what to do.
The run id, verifiable by access.
The Québec corpus awaits review, and the report says so.

lawyer.a: No. It applies written, sourced rules and shows the line behind every finding. It gives no legal advice, and the Québec corpus still awaits a lawyer's review: every report says so.

private.a: No. A document is visible to your account alone. A signed report can only be verified by the people you give access to, with a Yomizaka account, and every verification is logged.

ai.q: Does an AI judge my lease?
ai.a: The written rules decide. A model is consulted only for the single judgment question (the abusive clause), and the report says so; if the model is unavailable, the finding says « insufficient evidence » rather than guess.

rules.a: The Québec residential lease (ten rules), plus the French and Walloon residential leases, and the Québec supplier invoice (eight rules: date, total, GST and QST numbers, taxes, payment terms — from the federal regulation on input tax credit information, not yet reviewed by an accountant or a lawyer). For service contracts and employment contracts the rules are not written yet: those cases are marked « soon ».

engine.q: Where does the engine come from?
engine.a: Yomizaka runs on Orazaka, Krizaka's sovereign AI engine: each check is a run whose id is kept. Yomizaka's code is open (Apache-2.0).

access.a: Not yet: Yomizaka is in development and sign-up is closed. Write to us to talk about it.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: Yomizaka is in development: only the accounts our team creates can sign in. A document you upload is kept in Yomizaka's database (Toronto, Canada), visible to your account alone. When you ask for a check, the document — its text, or the PDF file — is sent to Orazaka, Krizaka's analysis engine, over HTTPS, and the result is kept with the run's id. Nothing is sold, shared or used to train a model. Deleting a document deletes its file, its text and its analyses. To ask a question or have your data removed, use the contact form.

report.title: Audit report — {name}
report.summary: {failures} blocking failure(s) out of {rules} rules checked.
report.toReview: Québec rules still to be reviewed by a lawyer: a demonstration report, not legal advice.
report.modelValue: Chosen by the Studio, not reported by the run: the Studio and its version above are the trace.
report.noPassage: No passage: the document says nothing on this point.
report.guarantees: This report is signed with Yomizaka's key (Ed25519, held by Krizaka). The signature covers the document's SHA-256, the jurisdiction and rules version, the Studio and its version, the Orazaka run id, the date of the check, every finding with its passage and article, and the full text of this report. If a single character of this file changes, verification fails.
report.notGuaranteed: It does not prove that the findings are legally right: Orazaka applies the rules, the Québec ruleset is still to be reviewed by a lawyer, and this is not legal advice. It does not prove that the run exists on Orazaka's side (only its operator can say), nor when the report was made beyond the check dates above: there is no independent time-stamp and no blockchain. What you trust is Krizaka, the holder of the signing key.
report.howToVerify: To verify it, sign in to Yomizaka and open {url} — only the people the report's owner gave access to can, with their Yomizaka account. Give it this file and, to confirm which document was checked, the original document.
report.footer: Yomizaka, a Krizaka product — analysis by Orazaka.
report.signatureBody: SHA-256 of the report's text (pages before this one)
report.signatureNote: The attestation — the payload, the text fingerprint and this signature — is also embedded in the PDF file. A member the owner gave access to checks it by giving this file to the verification page; any change to the text of the earlier pages makes it fail.

verify.okTitle: This report is authentic and unchanged.

reasons.NOT_A_REPORT: This is not a Yomizaka audit report: it has no signature block.
reasons.UNREADABLE: The signature block is damaged or not in a format Yomizaka knows.
reasons.BAD_SIGNATURE: The signature does not match the content: the report was modified or signed by another key.
reasons.ALTERED: The signature is valid for the original report, but the file is not that report any more: something was changed after signing.
reasons.UNKNOWN_KEY: It was signed by a key that is not this server's.
reasons.SPECIMEN: This report is a specimen: it proves nothing.

documentMatch.yes: The document you gave is the one that was checked.
documentMatch.no: The document you gave is NOT the one that was checked (its SHA-256 differs).
documentMatch.none: No document given: nothing says which file was checked except its SHA-256 above.

guarantees.a: The report was produced by Yomizaka's signing key, and not one character of it has changed since.
guarantees.b: It binds, in one signature, the document's SHA-256, the jurisdiction and rules version, the Studio and its version, the Orazaka run id, the check dates and every finding with its passage and article.
guarantees.c: Given the original document, it is the one that was checked.

limits.a: That the findings are right in law: Orazaka applies the rules, and the Québec ruleset is still to be reviewed by a lawyer. This is not legal advice.
limits.b: That the run exists on Orazaka's side: only its operator can confirm a run id.
limits.c: When the report was made, beyond the check dates it states: there is no independent time-stamp.
limits.d: Anything about the key holder: you trust Krizaka to keep the key. No blockchain, no third party.

verify.keyLead: Ed25519, SPKI in base64. With it you can verify a report without this site (for instance with OpenSSL on the signed text).
verify.devKey: This server uses the development key: its reports prove nothing.

examples.lead: Taken from a real check of a sample Québec lease, as it came back (the run is on the proof page).

items.a: « A security deposit of $1,450 at signing »: forbidden, only the first month may be asked in advance (C.c.Q., art. 1904).

items.c: « Children are not allowed in the dwelling »: a clause without effect (C.c.Q., arts. 1899 and 1901).
items.d: The rent and the notice of the lowest rent of the last twelve months (section G of the mandatory lease form): present, or to ask the landlord for.

c.text: A signed report with the run id, shared with your accountant or manager by giving them access.

keep.title: You upload the file
keep.text: It is kept as it is, visible to your account alone; its text layer is read for search.

read.title: Yomizaka examines it
read.text: The invoice against the rules written from the federal regulation, and the PDF as a file. The rules for supplier contracts will be added here once they exist. No model is ever called to judge your documents.

prove.title: You keep the proof
prove.text: Each finding keeps the id of its run; the report is signed, and only the people you give access to can verify it, with a Yomizaka account.

examples.title: What Yomizaka reads
examples.lead: The first example does not exist yet (soon); the last three already work.

items.a: Supplier contract: automatic renewal, penalties, exclusivity (soon).
items.b: Invoice: the supplier's GST and QST numbers well formed, the required mentions (available; the QST requirement itself is not encoded yet).
items.c: Edited invoice: signs of modification in the PDF (available).
items.d: The same invoice uploaded twice: recognised (available).

business.owl: The owl checks the invoice and the file today; it will read your contracts once their rules are written and sourced.

tenant.title: A request to check your application
tenant.lead: {landlord} asks your agreement to check your rental application. You decide: nothing is checked without your consent.
tenant.why: Why: the landlord is assessing your application for a dwelling.
tenant.notAsked: Never asked: social insurance number, bank details, employer, salary, criminal record.
tenant.whoSees: Who sees the result: you first; the landlord only if you pass it on.
tenant.retention: Duration: the result is deleted {days} days after your consent.
tenant.rights: You may decline (it is not an admission), contest the result, or not pass it on.
tenant.share: Pass it on to the landlord
tenant.demo: Demonstration provider: the data is fictitious.

state.consented: You consented. Here is the result: only you see it for now.
state.shared: You passed this result on to the landlord.
state.declined: You declined: nothing was checked, and the landlord is told so without more detail.
state.contested: You contested this result: the landlord does not see it.
state.expired: This request expired or its result was deleted.

landlord.title: Tenant application
landlord.lead: Ask an applicant's consent to check their payment history. They see the result first and decide whether to pass it on to you or contest it.
landlord.undertaking: I undertake to use these checks only to assess an application for a dwelling, to ask only what is necessary, and never to refuse an applicant on a discriminatory ground (Charter of human rights and freedoms; C.c.Q., art. 1899). I know an applicant may decline or contest, and that refusing to give unnecessary information is not a ground for rejection.
landlord.lawfulTitle: What the law lets you ask
landlord.lawful: The name, the current address, an identity document looked at without keeping a copy, the previous landlord's contact — and, with consent, a credit report. No social insurance number, bank details, employer or salary. Yomizaka offers no criminal-record check.
landlord.name: Applicant's name
landlord.created: Hand this link to the applicant (it will not be shown again):
landlord.hidden: The result is visible only once the applicant passes it on.
landlord.reviewNote: « To review » is not a verdict: talk to the applicant before any decision.
